page: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 5669 GB of local disk capacity with Premium Storage capability. There are no onboard GPUs, and the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier write bandwidth and strong read bandwidth. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform exceptionally well, with single-threaded gzip and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, processing 140.26 million operations per second.

Given its high core count, substantial memory, and massive local storage, this instance is highly cost-efficient for resource-dense deployments that require high local I/O and CPU throughput without the added expense of dedicated GPU hardware. It is highly suited for large relational databases, high-throughput web serving, enterprise-grade container orchestration, and CPU-based machine learning inference, where it exhibits top-tier text generation speeds.
